statement: In degree four, the lattice-path construction produces eleven generic real point constraints for which 564 of the 620 irreducible rational quartics are real. Therefore the degree-four maximum is at least 564 and at most 620; the general-degree maximum is not determined by this result.

answer.text: In degree four, the lattice-path construction produces eleven generic real point constraints for which 564 of the 620 irreducible rational quartics are real. Therefore the degree-four maximum is at least 564 and at most 620; the general-degree maximum is not determined by this result.
answer.qualification: Eleven generic real input points. The construction attains 564 real quartics; it does not establish the exact maximum.

source.version: Published Comptes Rendus Mathématique 336 (2003), 629–634, full PDF

scope: The degree-four member of the rational-plane-curve family, with all eleven input points real and generic.
notes: This fills only a specified family member and is orange at family level. It is a construction giving a lower bound on the maximum, not proof that 564 is maximal.
